clue.text: Playful talk of putting one article back into logo

indicators.note: putting something somewhere signals placing the following letters within another word
into says the logo word receives the letters inside it

parts.note: a badge is an emblem or logo
one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: back tells us the article is read in reverse order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A designer chats lightly about re-inserting an article into a company logo.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, teasing banter between people, a synonym of playful talk.

clue.text: Child's attachment to computer technology is a source of irritation

indicators.note: an attachment is joined on to something, so the child abbreviation is tacked after the technology letters

parts.note: IT is information technology
CH is the standard abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A parent laments their kid's obsession with gadgets as a constant annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin sensation that irritates and makes you want to scratch.

clue.text: Initially, Frances left off head of flower as too limp

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the name that follows

parts.note: the name supplies only its initial letter

indicators.note: off signals that something is removed from the flower word
head of points to the first letter as the part removed

parts.note: the poppy is a red flower

explanation.surface: Frances has cut the bloom off a wilting flower because it was droopy.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'as too' just link the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floppy hangs loosely without stiffness, a close synonym of limp.

clue.text: Stone at university provides a permanent way to make sculpture

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for the weight unit stone (14 pounds)
taken as written
taken as written
the permanent way is the track bed of a railway, abbreviated RY

explanation.surface: A campus railway line made of stone is turned into a sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permanent way' is the railway engineers' term for the finished track, so it gives RY for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is a collective noun for statues, that is, sculpture as a body of work.

clue.text: Period in cars or old powered bikes

indicators.note: in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: autos is an informal word for cars
a cycle is a recurring period of time

explanation.surface: A spell spent driving cars or riding early motorbikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocycles were early light motorcycles, pedal bikes fitted with a small engine.

clue.text: Missing sailors: 10 adrift

parts.note: ABs are able seamen

indicators.note: adrift means loose and out of place, so the letters of the number are rearranged

parts.note: the number ten spelt out

explanation.surface: Ten sailors are missing, lost at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 here is just the number, not a reference to clue 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, the same as missing.

clue.text: Its contents are undrinkable

definitions.meaning: suggests a bottle or vessel whose liquid is spoiled
really means the drink is locked away in view but cannot be reached

explanation.walkthrough: A tantalus is a locked stand holding decanters: the spirits are visible but cannot be drunk without the key, like the mythical Tantalus who could never reach the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The decanter stand is named after the Greek figure punished with drink always just out of reach.

clue.text: Role as rising governor

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes their promotion to the post of governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, now used for any petty ruler.

clue.text: Fingers doctor wrongly shut out

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits out, outside the doctor
wrongly means these letters are set in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic's fingers mistakenly shut out.
explanation.walkthrough: MB stands for Bachelor of Medicine, a British medical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a book is to leaf through it, so thumbs is a synonym of fingers as a verb.

clue.text: Food for an attractive girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prepared item of food served at a meal
second meaning: slang for a good-looking person

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as both a course on the menu and dated slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared meal, and colloquially a dish is a very good-looking person.

clue.text: One who asks for little in France and one in Ireland

parts.note: petit is French for small

indicators.note: in means the number word is set inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: the word one taken as written

explanation.surface: A beggar asks for small change in France and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner makes a formal request or plea, so is someone who asks.

clue.text: Covering article in reproduction

indicators.note: in places the article within the word for a reproduction

parts.note: a copy is a reproduction
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about covers on a reproduction piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering of cloth or other material.

clue.text: Give too much publicity about former model's earlier deliveries

indicators.note: earlier says the deliveries come before the rest of the pieces

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler
ex means former, as in an ex-partner
a model's job is to pose

explanation.surface: A tabloid publicises too much about a former model's past childbirths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests childbirth but is cricket: an over is six balls bowled. 'About' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexpose someone is to give them so much media attention that the public tires of them.

clue.text: Outlasts any market researchers

parts.note: read as Out plus lasts: out signals the anagram and is itself set aside, leaving lasts
taken as written into the mix

explanation.surface: One firm's market researchers outlast those of any rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split 'Outlasts' into 'Out' and 'lasts': 'Out' is the anagram signal and 'lasts any' supplies the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysts study data, and market analysts examine trends and consumer behaviour.

clue.text: Appear to get together after first evening

indicators.note: after says the joining word follows that single letter
first picks only the opening letter of the word evening

parts.note: the word evening supplies only its first letter
to merge is to combine or come together

explanation.surface: Friends turn up to meet after the first evening of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, which is to appear.

clue.text: EEC doing badly? It's wholesale murder!

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are done wrongly and so scrambled

parts.note: the letters of these two words are taken as written and mixed

explanation.surface: A satirical jab: is the European Economic Community performing so poorly that it's slaughter?
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Genocide is the deliberate killing of a whole people, murder on a mass scale.

clue.text: Run to west coast city with minor legislation

parts.note: in cricket a bye is a run scored without the ball touching the bat
LA, Los Angeles, is on the US west coast

explanation.surface: Someone runs off to California to deal with local regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like it gives W, but it belongs to the city; the W comes from 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: A byelaw is a rule made by a local authority, a lesser law than a statute.

clue.text: Cautious about tirade on assurance

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes around the other

parts.note: wary means careful or cautious
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A customer is wary of a salesman's angry speech about a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee, an assurance that goods will be repaired or replaced.

clue.text: Fellow telling tales of getting the kite up

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the -ing form, as in flying a kite

parts.note: lying is telling untruths, or tales

explanation.surface: A man fibs about how he managed to launch his kite.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying a kite means launching it into the air and keeping it aloft.

clue.text: Gather the road is cut back — extremely annoying!

parts.note: to gather is to infer or deduce

indicators.note: back means the shortened word is read in reverse
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: Someone learns their road is being dug up again and is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal literally means hellish, and colloquially describes something tiresome or irritating.

clue.text: Bear free in American city not far away

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: the word bear taken as written to be mixed

explanation.surface: A bear is loose in a US city, close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby is an adverb meaning close at hand, the opposite of far away.

clue.text: Take cover from ruins about to start erupting

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around and reshuffled

parts.note: the word ruins taken as written to be mixed

indicators.note: start picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the word erupting supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: People hide from ruins that are about to blow up like a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to take out cover, a policy protecting against loss.

clue.text: The pressure's the same all along the line

definitions.meaning: sounds like a remark about uniform stress, but is literally about air pressure
an idiom for throughout, but here an actual line on a weather map

explanation.walkthrough: An isobar is a line on a weather chart joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists draw these contour lines to connect places with equal barometric readings.

clue.text: Mafia leader, when accepting composer, dropped one cup of coffee

indicators.note: accepting means the leader's title takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a capo is a Mafia boss

indicators.note: dropped means a letter is let fall out of the composer's name

parts.note: Puccini was the Italian opera composer
one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss meets an Italian composer, who drops his coffee cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an Italian espresso coffee topped with frothed milk.

clue.text: Old turmoil about a lot to carry

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
turmoil suggests the letters are thrown into confusion and rearranged

parts.note: the word old taken as written to be jumbled
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly person is upset about having so much to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is a quantity carried at one time, a burden.

clue.text: Pinch a free journey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to steal, as a verb
second meaning: a ride in someone's car without paying

explanation.walkthrough: Both are everyday senses: to lift is to steal, and a lift is a ride you are given.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is slang for steal, and in British usage a lift is a free ride in a car.

clue.text: Swore at a journalist taking coach

indicators.note: taking means the outer pieces take in the vehicle word

parts.note: taken as written
ED is short for editor
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A reporter on a coach trip cursed at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone verbally is to insult or curse them, so abused can mean swore at.

clue.text: The writing on the wall?

definitions.meaning: suggests an ominous sign of doom, the idiom 'the writing on the wall'
taken literally means words painted or scrawled on a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means a warning of coming disaster, but read literally it describes words daubed on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are drawings or words scratched or sprayed on public surfaces.
